true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Duplicate downsize definition removes 4-arg overload

In app/models/optimized_image.rb lines 145 and 149 there are two `self.downsize` definitions: one taking `(from,to,max_width,max_height,opts)` and one taking `(from,to,dimensions,opts)`. In Ruby the last definition wins, so the 4-arg version is dead code. Any existing caller using `downsize(from,to,width,height)` now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). Keep one method supporting both arities or different names.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores per-type site settings

In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js line 182, validateUploadedFile now uses hardcoded `10*1024` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb']`. The old code used max_image_size_kb for images and max_attachment_size_kb for attachments. Now both types are limited to 10MB: sites allowing e.g. 50MB attachments will incorrectly reject them client-side, and sites with e.g. 1-2MB limits will incorrectly allow them client-side only to fail later on the server with a confusing message showing 10240.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
In-place image downsize corrupts tempfile and uses stale size

In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 67, `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` uses the same path for input and output. External `convert from[0] ... to` can truncate/replace the output before reading finishes, corrupting the upload. After the external rewrite the open Tempfile descriptor may still point at the old inode while `tempfile.size` is stale, so the `while tempfile.size > limit` check and final `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size)` can use wrong size/bytes. Return value is also ignored, so on convert failure it loops 5 times doing expensive convert+ImageOptim work then fails late. Use a separate temp file, check success, and stat `File.size(path)`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

false_positives.candidate:
413 error handler shows wrong hardcoded limit

In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js line 246, the 413 handler now reports hardcoded `10*1024` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. The displayed max_size_kb will be wrong whenever the admin configured a different limit, misleading users about why the upload was rejected.

API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB bypasses admin setting

In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 55, FileHelper.download limit was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to hardcoded `10.megabytes`. If admin sets a smaller limit the server still fetches/downloads/processes up to 10MB (extra bandwidth/disk/CPU and policy bypass), and if admin allows larger than 10MB the download is needlessly truncated/failed.

Large SVG uploads sent through ImageMagick rasterizer

In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 64, the auto-downsize guard is true for any `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` including `.svg`, and then runs `OptimizedImage.downsize` via `convert -resize`. Elsewhere in app/models/optimized_image.rb lines 45-47 SVGs are explicitly excluded from ImageMagick (just copied) because convert rasterizes them. A large SVG over the limit will therefore be mangled/converted instead of preserved or rejected; SVGs should be skipped in the downsize loop.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation crashes on nil host

In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the before_validation block calls self.host.sub! twice without checking presence. If host is nil or missing (e.g. admin submits blank host), this raises NoMethodError on nil instead of failing validation. Consequence: POST/PUT to Admin::EmbeddableHostsController with blank host returns 500 instead of a 422 validation error and breaks the admin UI error path.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Update/destroy do not handle missing record

In app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update does EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first then calls save_host(host), and destroy does the same lookup then host.destroy. If the id does not exist host is nil, so save_host(nil) calls nil.host= and nil.destroy raises NoMethodError. Consequence: requesting a non-existent id causes a 500 exception instead of a 404/not-found response.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host lookup is case-sensitive and ignores port mismatch

In app/models/embeddable_host.rb record_for_host does where("lower(host) = ?", host) where host is uri.host as-is, without downcasing, so lower(stored) is compared to mixed-case input and uppercase URLs miss. Additionally validation allows host:port but lookup extracts uri.host without port, so a stored example.com:3000 never equals example.com. Consequence: legitimate embed URLs are rejected as invalid referer host.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration inserts unnormalized hosts that never match

In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the loop inserts raw setting lines h directly, bypassing EmbeddableHost normalization that strips scheme and path. Old settings commonly contain values like http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234, so the new table ends up with scheme/path included. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares URI.host (bare hostname) to the stored string, so those migrated rows never match. Consequence: embedding silently stops working after upgrade.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator file contents are swapped

In spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb the file now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines Fabricator(:category) and related categories. The contents are in the wrong files. It still loads but is misleading and will confuse maintainers; the definitions should be moved back to their matching filenames.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration SQL-injects host value

In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds INSERT with string interpolation: VALUES ('#{h}', ... ) where h comes from the old embeddable_hosts site setting split by newline. A host containing a single quote breaks the SQL and allows SQL injection/error. Consequence: migration can fail or execute unintended SQL; must use quoting/sanitization or ActiveRecord models.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration assumes site_settings rows exist

In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb line 9 does execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name='embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i without nil checks. On a fresh install where embed_category was never persisted there are zero rows, so [0] is nil and ['id'] raises. Consequence: rake db:migrate fails for new databases.

false_positives.candidate:
No real coverage for new admin endpoints

In spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and embedding_controller_spec.rb the only test is that the controller is a subclass of AdminController. There is no coverage for create/update/destroy validation, 404 handling, auth (admin vs moderator/anon), category fallback, or serialization. Consequence: regressions in the new embedding admin API, including the nil-handling and validation bugs above, will not be caught.

_hydrateEmbedded crashes on null plural ids

In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6 _hydrateEmbedded for keys matching *_ids does obj[k].map(...) with no array guard. If the server serializes an empty association as null/undefined instead of [], this throws TypeError. Consequence: store.find/findAll for any model with a null plural id field crashes the client; should check Array.isArray or fallback to [].

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when TopicUser row is missing

In TopicsController#unsubscribe the code does TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) then immediately calls tu.notification_level. find_by returns nil when the user has no row for the topic, for example a user who was @mentioned or mailed but never visited. That raises NoMethodError on nil and returns 500 instead of unsubscribing. It must handle nil via TopicUser.change or find-or-create.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Direct TopicUser save bypasses reason, timestamp and live update

The action assigns tu.notification_level and calls tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change used by set_notifications. That skips setting notifications_changed_at, notifications_reason_id, and publishing MessageBus notification_level_change. The result is stale audit fields and open topic pages/tracking state that do not update live, diverging from all other notification-level changes.

List-Unsubscribe header not updated to per-topic URL

The email body now includes a per-topic unsubscribe_url, but header_args still sets List-Unsubscribe to only user_preferences_url even when unsubscribe_url is present. Email clients that use the header for one-click unsubscribe will send the user to generic preferences instead of unsubscribing from the topic, making header and body inconsistent and defeating the feature for those clients.

No test verifies per-topic unsubscribe URL or controller behavior

The spec adds unsubscribe_url to the builder fixture but only asserts the generic user_preferences_url in the body and presence of the header. Nothing asserts the body/header contain the per-topic unsubscribe_url, and there is no controller test for TopicsController#unsubscribe covering missing TopicUser, downgrade-vs-mute, login/token, or GET side effects, so the bugs above ship undetected.

Per-topic email link requires login so logged-out clicks fail

TopicsController#unsubscribe is in the ensure_logged_in list, yet the URL is mailed as a one-click unsubscribe link. A recipient who clicks while logged out, on another device, or after session expiry is redirected to login and never unsubscribed. The existing global unsubscribe uses email/unsubscribe/:key token auth for this reason; the per-topic link needs token auth or it is dead on arrival for logged-out users.

State-changing unsubscribe on GET enables CSRF/prefetch unsubscribe

TopicsController#unsubscribe is routed as GET in config/routes.rb but mutates notification_level and saves. Browsers, email link scanners, and crawlers prefetch GETs, and an attacker can embed the URL as an image to force a logged-in victim's browser to unsubscribe with no CSRF token. Safe methods must not mutate; GET should render confirmation and mutation should require POST/PUT.

Watching/tracking users are only downgraded, not unsubscribed

The code sets notification_level to regular when it is greater than regular, else to muted. A watching (3) or tracking (2) user who clicks the email promise to stop receiving notifications about this topic is left at regular (1), which still generates reply/mention/watch emails. It takes a second visit to reach muted. It should set muted directly for an email unsubscribe.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Email validation mutates DB causing double-counted block stats

EmailValidator.validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count, updates last_match_at and saves. Validation is supposed to be side-effect free. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, each of which runs validations, so a single blocked signup attempt increments the counter twice. Any other call to valid? (admin UI, console, tests) also mutates stats even if the user is never saved. Consequence is inflated match_count and misleading last_match_at, making abuse metrics unreliable.

true_positives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Domain whitelist regex not anchored allows subdomain spoof

email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(domains)") with no end anchor and matches by substring. A whitelist entry like example.com therefore matches user@example.com.evil.com because the string contains @example.com, even though the real domain is evil.com. The whitelisted user passes validation incorrectly. Similarly a blacklist can over-match. The regex should be anchored to the end of the address and handle domain boundaries correctly.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive allowing bypass

BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up with BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first using the raw user-supplied string with no downcasing or stripping, and the model validates uniqueness case-sensitively. Email delivery treats addresses case-insensitively in practice and users can add case changes or whitespace. An attacker blocked as bad@spam.com can sign up as BAD@spam.com or Bad@spam.com and miss the block, and admins can create logically duplicate block entries. Should normalize emails on save and lookup, e.g. with Email.downcase and strip.

false_positives.candidate:
Non-atomic match_count increment loses concurrent updates

BlockedEmail.should_block? does read-modify-write: record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save. Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email can interleave reads and overwrite each other, losing increments. The save also runs full validations including an extra uniqueness SELECT. Consequence is lost counts under load and wasted queries. Should use an atomic increment such as increment_counter or update_counters that bypasses validations.

Shared mutable rejectedEmails array on prototype

CreateAccountController is extended with rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) as a prototype property. That single array instance is shared by all instances of the controller. Pushes of server-rejected emails leak across modal instances and persist after close/reopen, causing stale addresses to be treated as rejected for future unrelated signups. Mutable defaults should be created per-instance in init or reset when the modal opens.

Wrong Ember dependent key prevents rejected-email UI update

emailValidation is declared dependent on accountEmail and rejectedEmails.@each. In Ember, @each observes properties of array items, not array membership; pushing a string with pushObject does not invalidate the computed property. The correct key is rejectedEmails.[] or length. After the server rejects an email and it is pushed into rejectedEmails, the validation still returns ok and submitDisabled stays false until the user edits the email, so the user can immediately resubmit the same blocked email repeatedly.

change_email action bypasses blocked-email check

UsersController#change_email lowercases the new address, checks only whether another User already owns it, then creates an EmailToken and enqueues authorization without ever running EmailValidator or checking BlockedEmail.should_block?. An address rejected at signup as blocked can therefore still be adopted by an existing account via the email-change flow. Consequence is the blocklist is ineffective after account creation. The new address should be validated the same way as signup.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsafe open of feed URL with no error handling

In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 29, code does SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) using Kernel#open/open-uri on an admin setting with no URI validation, timeout, or rescue. It allows file:// or pipe arguments in older Ruby, follows redirects arbitrarily (SSRF), and any network/DNS/parse error raises out of the scheduled job. Consequence is job failure, Sidekiq noise, and potential local-file read or internal-network fetch.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check is reversed

In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js line 17, the check is discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)===-1, i.e. does discourseUrl contain e.origin, instead of checking e.origin equals the Discourse origin. Any origin that is a prefix/substring passes, e.g. discourseUrl http://example.com contains attacker origin http://example.co. Consequence is a malicious page can send discourse-resize messages to control iframe height, and the pattern invites broader message forgery if more types are added.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage targetOrigin uses full referer

In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb line 11, code calls parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>') where request.referer is the full URL including path/query, not an origin. The postMessage spec requires scheme+host+port; passing a full URL means the message is never delivered (or throws). When referer is nil it passes empty string which throws. Consequence is embed auto-resize is broken and relies on attacker-controlled header for security boundary.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Stored XSS via unescaped URL and unsanitized raw_html In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13, TopicEmbed.import interpolates the attacker-controlled url directly into HTML: "#{url}" with only a /^https?:\/\// prefix check. A URL like http://embeddable_host/'> passes the check and has the allowed host, so TopicRetriever will accept it. The resulting HTML is stored as a Post with cook_method raw_html (line 22) which bypasses all cooking/sanitization in Post#cook, and rendered with raw post.cooked in app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 19. Consequence is persistent stored XSS executed in browsers viewing the embed or topic.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Nil feed content crashes entire poll

In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35, poll_feed does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub). RSS 2.0 items often have no content element (only description/title) and SimpleRSS returns nil for i.content. Calling scrub on nil raises NoMethodError with no rescue, aborting the loop. Consequence is one legacy item prevents all feed items from being imported/updated and fails the hourly scheduled job.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Disqus replies pass ignored cooked param

In lib/tasks/disqus.thor line 160, the importer builds attrs with raw: p[:cooked], cooked: p[:cooked]. PostCreator.setup_post only reads raw and computes cooked via Post#cook; the cooked key is ignored. First post is created as raw_html via TopicEmbed.import_remote but replies are created as regular markdown posts containing raw HTML. Consequence is Disqus HTML is escaped/sanitized inconsistently, breaking formatting and losing intended rendering.

Mutates caller string with <<

In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13, import does contents << "\n<hr>..." which mutates the caller's String in place instead of duping. If the caller reuses the string it gets a second footer on retry, and frozen strings raise RuntimeError. Consequence is duplicated imported-from footers, surprising side effects, and crashes with frozen literals.

No handling for missing/deleted embed post

In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 32, the update path does post = embed.post then PostRevisor.new(post).revise! with no nil check. If the post/topic was deleted, trashed, or never created due to failed PostCreator, post is nil and revise! raises NoMethodError. There is also no check that revise! succeeded before embed.update_column(:content_sha1). Consequence is poll/retrieve jobs crash mid-loop and sha can diverge from actual post content.

Non-atomic throttle with raw URL as Redis key

In lib/topic_retriever.rb line 27, retrieved_recently? does $redis.setnx(key,1) then separate $redis.expire(key,60). If the process crashes between calls the key never expires and that embed_url is throttled forever. The key is "retrieved:#{@embed_url}" using unbounded user input, allowing huge keys and memory abuse. Consequence is permanent denial of retrieval for a URL and Redis bloat; should use SET NX EX atomically and hash the URL.

Spec mocks TopicRetriever but controller enqueues job

In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb line 40, the test expects TopicRetriever.new/retrieve directly, while app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 15 does Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic,...). If test jobs run inline the mock may accidentally pass, otherwise it fails, and in production the async path with user_id/embed_url args, throttling, and host validation is never asserted. Consequence is the real enqueue contract is untested and regressions will not be caught.

absolutize_urls raises on malformed URL

In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 57, absolutize_urls does URI(url) with no rescue. Any malformed embed_url or feed link raises URI::InvalidURIError and aborts import/revise and the calling job. It also only handles href/src starting with / and mishandles protocol-relative //host/path, leaving broken or wrong absolute URLs. Consequence is single bad URL fails feed poll or embed retrieval.

downcase on possibly nil embed_by_username

In lib/topic_retriever.rb line 49, fetch_http does SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase with no blank check. If the setting is nil (default/unset in tests and fresh installs) this raises NoMethodError. Unlike PollFeed#execute which guards present?, every embed retrieval via RetrieveTopic hits this. Consequence is all embed fetches raise instead of no-op until admin configures the user.

import_remote uses open without require or rescue

In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48, import_remote does open(url).read without requiring open-uri in that file and without begin/rescue/timeout/validation. If open-uri was not already loaded it does local file open, and any 404/timeout/invalid URL raises. Called from TopicRetriever.fetch_http and Disqus import, the exception bubbles and fails the RetrieveTopic job. Consequence is embed retrieval never completes and repeated retries on every embed view.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name missing ? so filter is never called

In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb the serializer defines def include_website_name without a question mark. ActiveModel::Serializer checks include_<attr>? to decide whether to include an attribute, as used elsewhere in the same file for include_stats?, include_suspend_reason?, etc. Because the ? is missing the method is ignored, the website.present? guard is dead code, and website_name is always serialized even when website is blank or nil.

false_positives.candidate:
Host comparison is case-sensitive

In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb website_host is compared to Discourse.current_hostname with == and ends_with? without downcasing. DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, so a user website like http://EXAMPLE.COM/foo on an instance at example.com will be treated as an external domain and shown without path, producing inconsistent display for the same host.

Untrusted-attributes test omits website_name

In spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb the TL0 anonymous test lists bio_raw, bio_cooked, bio_excerpt, location, website, profile_background, card_background but not website_name. It therefore cannot catch that website_name is still serialized for TL0 users seen as anonymous while website is hidden.

website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous hiding for website

In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb website is listed in untrusted_attributes so it is hidden from anonymous viewers when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) is true for TL0 users. website_name was added to attributes on line 43 but was not added to untrusted_attributes. As a result a TL0 user's website host plus path is still sent as website_name even when website itself is suppressed, leaking the private profile field the restriction is meant to hide.

website_name drops port, query string and fragment

In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb website_name is built as website_host + URI(website.to_s).path in all three branches. That discards port, query string and fragment, so http://example.com/page?x=1#y and http://example.com:8080/page are both displayed as example.com/page. Two distinct user URLs become indistinguishable and the displayed text does not match the linked href, contrary to the stated goal of showing the complete path.

true_positives.golden_comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embedded reply author color light value flipped from 30% to 70%

In desktop/topic-post.scss line 291 the rule .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The light-theme value should have been preserved as 30% with dark counterpart 70% to sum to 100% like every other conversion and like the matching quote-title rule in common/base/topic-post.scss. true_positives.golden_comment: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
add/remove member actions require :group_id but route and client supply :id

Admin JS calls PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members.json with only user_id/usernames in the body. The Rails member route `delete/put 'members'` under `resources :groups` supplies the group id as params[:id], not params[:group_id]. Both add_members (line 66) and remove_member (line 85) do Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i), so every real request raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and the admin add/remove member feature is broken. Specs pass only because they call the action directly with group_id, bypassing routing.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

false_positives.candidate:
Adding members splits on comma without stripping whitespace

add_members does usernames.split(',').each with no strip. Input like 'alice, bob' from a user-selector leaves a leading space on the second name, so User.find_by_username(' bob') returns nil and that user is silently skipped while the endpoint still returns success. The admin thinks all users were added when only a subset was.

Group create ignores alias_level sent by client

The JS Group.asJSON() sends name, alias_level and visible, and update handles alias_level, but create only assigns name and visible. A group created with a non-default alias level silently loses that choice and gets the default, requiring a second update to fix.

Public group members page only loads first page with no pagination

The public members route now sets the model to the Group object and calls model.findMembers() once, which defaults to limit 50 offset 0. There is no next/previous UI on the public members template. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members, so any group with more than 50 members now permanently shows only the first 50 with no way to see the rest.

Unbounded limit/offset params allow DoS and invalid queries

Members action does limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset = params[:offset].to_i with no clamping. A caller can request limit=1000000 to force loading huge numbers of users into memory, or negative limit/offset which produces SQL errors or surprising results. Limit should be clamped to a sane max (e.g. 1..200) and offset to >=0.

remove_member uses low-level association delete bypassing domain logic

remove_member does group.users.delete(user_id) while the add path uses group.add(user) and the old code used group.remove(user). Direct association delete bypasses Group model callbacks and counter maintenance, then calls group.save redundantly. This risks stale user_count and missed side effects, and is inconsistent with the add path.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
DB lookup on every fallback miss

In config/initializers/i18n.rb FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale on every lookup. The I18n fallback backend calls fallbacks[locale] for every missing key, so every untranslated key does a SiteSetting read in the hot translation path instead of using a cached value, adding Redis/DB overhead to pages with many missing keys.

Fallback files only preloaded on web requests

In app/controllers/application_controller.rb set_locale calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! to load the user locale, site default, and :en. But lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb I18n.translate only does load_locale(config.locale) for the current locale. Any I18n.t outside a controller request — Sidekiq jobs, mailers, background email rendering, console, rake — never preloads the fallback locales, so a key missing in the current locale returns translation-missing even though it exists in the site default or English.

Nil default_locale crashes fallback instead of falling back

In config/initializers/i18n.rb FallbackLocaleList#[] does [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact. If SiteSetting.default_locale is nil or blank the .to_sym call raises NoMethodError before .compact ever runs, so the compact is dead code. Any missing translation then raises instead of falling back to :en, turning a translation miss into a 500 during setup, migrations, or if the setting is cleared.

Translation LRU cache ignores fallback chain

In lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb I18n.translate caches with key "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}", which omits SiteSetting.default_locale and the fallback list. A miss resolved via fallback (e.g. fr -> de -> en) is cached under the request locale alone. If the admin later changes SiteSetting.default_locale, the cached fallback value is still served until I18n.reload! or process restart, showing the old language.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative queryset slicing is unsupported and attacker-triggerable

In src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 882, when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0 the code executes list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySets explicitly do not support negative indexing/slicing and raise AssertionError, contrary to the inline comment claiming Django handles it automatically. Cursor strings of the form value:offset:is_prev are client-controlled via Cursor.from_string, so a caller of the new optimized_pagination=true path can craft a negative-offset cursor to trigger an unhandled 500 (DoS). If the slice ever operated on a list, negative start would wrap around and return tail rows outside the requested page, breaking completeness of audit logs.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime ordering

In src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 840, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor(value))/int(math.ceil(value)) on the sort-key attribute. The only caller added in this PR (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py line 80) uses order_by="-datetime", so value is a datetime.datetime, not a number, which raises TypeError on every page. Even if it did not raise, value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value while build_queryset compares it against a datetime column with >=/<=, producing type-mismatched SQL or wrong pages. Consequence: the new optimized path always 500s or returns incorrect audit-log pages.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

false_positives.candidate:
BasePaginator still passes negative offsets for prev cursors

In src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 182, BasePaginator.get_result now does start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset, so forward pagination clamps negatives but prev-page (is_prev=True) pagination passes the raw negative offset to queryset[start_offset:stop]. This still hits Django's unsupported negative-slice path and raises AssertionError on a crafted prev cursor, turning all existing cursor-paginated endpoints into a 500 instead of rejecting the cursor. The later check len(results) == offset + limit + extra also uses the negative offset, so prev-page extra-row trimming is mathematically wrong even if slicing succeeded, causing duplicated or missing rows.

Untested privileged pagination path for compliance-critical logs

In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py lines 70-83, a new public query parameter optimized_pagination=true switches audit-log listing from DateTimePaginator to OptimizedCursorPaginator for superusers or members with global access. No tests are added for the branch or for OptimizedCursorPaginator, despite audit logs being compliance-critical. Consequence: a broken datetime-incompatible paginator with unsafe offset handling is exposed to privileged viewers without coverage, risking outages and incomplete/duplicated audit history going undetected.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative-offset slicing crashes instead of paginating

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 enables queryset[start_offset:stop] with negative start_offset when enable_advanced_features is true, claiming Django handles negative slicing and that it is safe because permissions are checked at queryset level. Django QuerySets reject negative slice bounds with AssertionError, unlike Python lists. A client-supplied cursor such as 0:-10:0 therefore raises an unhandled exception. Consequence: crafted cursor causes 500 errors (DoS) and the safety comment is false; other paginators correctly raise BadPaginationError for offset<0.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
BasePaginator allows negative slice that crashes

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 computes start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset and then does queryset[start_offset:stop], so a prev cursor with negative offset is passed directly to Django. Django QuerySets reject negative slice bounds with AssertionError (negative indexing is not supported), unlike Python lists, while sibling paginators raise BadPaginationError for offset<0. A client-supplied cursor like 0:-5:1 therefore causes an unhandled exception. Consequence: any authenticated user can trigger 500 errors on BasePaginator-based endpoints via crafted cursor (DoS).

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks datetime ordering

When used with order_by='-datetime' as in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, the attribute is a datetime object so math.floor raises TypeError, and build_queryset compares a datetime column to an int instead of converting via datetime.fromtimestamp like DateTimePaginator does. true_positives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Test factory blindly trusts client-supplied sample rate

_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling copies client-controlled contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate into normalized_data[sample_rate] with no validation. It uses if client_sample_rate so rate 0 is dropped, swallows all errors with bare except pass, overwrites any existing sample_rate, and accepts out-of-range or non-numeric values. Tests built on it therefore validate upsampling against arbitrary client-supplied weights (a client sending 0.001 would inflate counts 1000x) that production ingestion must reject, making endpoint tests unrealistic and hiding a trust-boundary issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unstable Python hash() used for shared cache key

The eligibility cache key is built with hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))). Python documents hash() as unstable across processes and versions (hash randomization), so the same project set maps to different keys in different workers/restarts. Since the cache is shared (memcached/Redis), cross-process lookups miss and each process creates its own key for the same projects, defeating the 60s caching and bloating the cache. Use a stable encoding such as comma-joined sorted IDs or hashlib.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of executed scoped_dataset

_get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset, the dataset actually queried. The dashboard-split logic calls it with different datasets (scoped_dataset vs discover for errors-only and transactions-only subqueries). The eligibility check passes the outer dataset closed over from get(), not scoped_dataset, so an errors-only subquery run on discover can be judged as a metrics/transactions query and skip upsampling, or a transaction query can be judged as errors and get upsampled, returning wrong counts.

false_positives.candidate:
60-second eligibility cache returns stale upsampling decisions

is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches allowlist eligibility (True/False) for 60 seconds keyed only by org and projects. If the project allowlist changes, queries for up to 60s use the old decision and return raw count() when scaled upsampled_count() was required or vice versa, with errors scaled by 1/sample_rate (e.g. 10x). The invalidate_upsampling_cache helper defined in the same file is never called in the PR, so there is no invalidation path.

Column transform only handles exact count() and hardcodes alias

transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites a column whose lowercased stripped value equals exactly count(). Variants such as count() as foo, count_if, count_unique, or equations containing count() are left as raw counts, so a request mixes raw and scaled series in one response. When it does match it forces upsampled_count() as count, discarding the caller's alias and injecting AS syntax into RPC y_axes paths that expect bare aggregates, risking validation failures or mislabeled series.

Error-focus check reads original HTTP query and only matches event.type:error

_is_error_focused_query inspects request.GET.get("query"), the original HTTP parameter, not the query string argument actually sent to Snuba. Dashboard-split code re-executes _get_event_stats with rewritten queries like (query) AND !event.type:transaction for errors and (query) AND event.type:transaction for transactions while request.GET is unchanged. The check also only matches substring event.type:error, so a discover errors-only query built from !event.type:transaction is treated as non-error and undercounts, while a transactions-only subquery issued when the HTTP query contained event.type:error is treated as error and sums sample_weight which does not exist for transactions.

Internal upsampled_count function exposed as public API

SnQLFunction upsampled_count is registered without private=True, unlike neighboring internal aggregates. That makes upsampled_count() directly queryable by any Discover user. Because it sums the internal sample_weight column, callers can invoke it on non-allowlisted projects or datasets where the column is missing or 1 and receive misleading scaled numbers, and can probe internal sampling state. Internal upsampling helpers should be private.

Main upsampling entry point and cache behavior untested

The test class exercises only private helpers (_are_all_projects_error_upsampled, transform, _is_error_focused_query, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform) and never calls the public is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects. Cache-key construction, 60s staleness, hash instability, and dataset/request interaction therefore have zero unit coverage, and the SnubaParams fixture with start=None/end=None is never used, so the caching bugs shipped in this PR cannot be caught.

upsampled_count sums nullable sample_weight without fallback and truncates

The new Discover function is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no null handling. Any error row without sample_weight (events written before sampling, backfills, mixed data) contributes 0/NULL instead of 1, so buckets undercount and can collapse to 0. toInt64 also truncates fractional weights, so a rate that does not evenly divide 1 (e.g. 0.33 -> weight ~3.03) is systematically biased low on every bucket. It should sum coalesced weights with rounding, e.g. sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1)).

In packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx the cache timestamp uses new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) ignoring the user's locale from useLocale. Users in other locales see MM/DD/YYYY format inconsistent with the rest of the app. Pass the current locale instead of hardcoding en-US.

false_positives.candidate:
Cache status includes expired entries

In packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only returns rows with expiresAt >= now. The UI therefore shows Cache Status / Last updated even when all rows for that credential are expired and will never be used, misleading users and offering Delete cached data for dead data. Delete-cache success never refreshes cache status

In packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx the deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only shows a toast and calls optional onSuccess prop, while disconnectMutation invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations onSettled. true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fire-and-forget forEach for reminder cancellation can lose updates

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts updatedBookings.forEach calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder which are async and return promises, but forEach does not await them and they are not added to prismaPromises. The same pattern exists in handleNewBooking, viewer/bookings requestReschedule, and viewer/workflows. Consequence: the API can return and the serverless function can freeze before the prisma update to cancelled=true or delete completes, so cancellations are silently lost and reminder emails/SMS are still sent.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
immediateDelete path cancels SendGrid but never deletes/flags DB row

In packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true does a SendGrid cancel then returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row and without setting cancelled=true. Callers like handleNewBooking reschedule rely on this to clean up the old booking's reminders. Consequence: stale rows with scheduled=true and valid referenceId remain linked to the old bookingUid forever until past-date cleanup, DB state says scheduled while SendGrid says cancelled, and the cron cancel query on cancelled=true will never pick them up.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancel query lacks method/scheduled filter and can SendGrid-cancel SMS

In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts remindersToCancel queries only cancelled=true and scheduledDate lte now+1h, with no filter on method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId not null. It then unconditionally POSTs batch_id to SendGrid scheduled_sends. Consequence: any SMS/Twilio reminder ever marked cancelled or any unscheduled row with null referenceId would trigger a SendGrid call with wrong/null batch_id, causing errors that trigger the whole-batch abort, and SMS reminders would be deleted without ever calling Twilio cancel.

Reschedule uses immediate SendGrid cancel defeating deferred-cancel fix

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts the reschedule path calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true) which does an immediate SendGrid POST cancel. The PR description says the fix is to only set cancelled=true and let the cron within one hour do the SendGrid cancel to avoid the 100 pending-cancellations limit. Consequence: reschedules again do immediate cancels under load, reintroducing the SendGrid limit failure that caused emails to still be sent, and is inconsistent with the cancel path which correctly defers.

SMS DB delete skipped when Twilio cancel throws

In packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts deleteScheduledSMSReminder does await twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId) then await prisma.workflowReminder.delete inside the same try. If cancelSMS throws (already sent, unknown SID, Twilio error) the delete is skipped and the error is only logged. Consequence: the WorkflowReminder row for a cancelled/rescheduled booking is left in the DB indefinitely and will never be retried, leaking data and leaving incorrect scheduled state.

Single try around cancel loop aborts all remaining cancels and drops queued deletes

In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts the code fetches remindersToCancel then enters one try block that loops with await client.request for each reminder and only after the loop does Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete). If any single SendGrid POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends fails (bad batch_id, already sent, network), execution jumps to catch, remaining reminders are never attempted and the delete promises already pushed are never awaited. Consequence: one bad reminder blocks cancellation of all others in that cron run, so cancelled/rescheduled bookings still get emails, which is the bug this PR claims to fix.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:

If any single import() rejects or getCalendar throws, the whole Promise.all rejects and getCachedResults throws, discarding availability for all other healthy calendars. true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletions unawaited

In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) is used. Array.forEach does not await async callbacks, so the await getCalendar() and subsequent calendar.deleteEvent()/deleteMeeting() promises are never awaited and their rejections escape the surrounding try/catch. In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts line 460 bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(...) }) runs async callbacks without awaiting them. apiDeletes is later consumed by Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)). Eager dynamic imports load all apps upfront anyway

In packages/app-store/index.ts lines 3-30 the object literal evaluates import("./applecalendar"), import("./googlecalendar"), etc. immediately when the module is first imported. Consequence: no cold-start or bundle-size benefit is achieved while every getCalendar/getVideoAdapter now pays an extra async tick and error-handling burden; true laziness requires functions or getters like applecalendar: () => import(...).

getCalendarCredentials now returns promises in sync return value

In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts line 28 const calendar = getCalendar(credential) now stores a Promise<Calendar|null> because getCalendar became async, but getCalendarCredentials itself stayed synchronous and still returns [{integration, credential, calendar}]. Any consumer not updated to await item.calendar will treat a Promise object as truthy Calendar, so checks like if (!calendar) never trigger and calls like calendar.listCalendars fail. Only getConnectedCalendars was updated to await; other importers break.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours end uses start time so events overrunning closing time pass

In the working-hours fallback both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute()`. The end should be derived from slot end time (start + eventLength). As written an event that starts inside working hours but ends outside is still considered available, allowing bookings past closing time.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dayjs equality uses === so full-day unavailable override never matches

In checkIfIsAvailable the code tests `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect an unavailable-day override where start equals end. Dayjs instances are objects, so === compares identity and is always false. The branch never fires, dateOverrideExist stays true, and the function later returns true, so a day the host marked as fully unavailable becomes bookable.

false_positives.candidate:
Active overrides filtered only by start instant misses overlapping day

activeOverrides keeps an override only if `dayjs.utc(override.start)` falls inside the invitee day. An override that overlaps the day but starts on an adjacent day due to timezone shift or an evening interval spanning midnight is dropped, so the day falls back to regular working hours and shows wrong availability. The later hour/minute math also drops day overflow, assigning shifted times to the wrong day.

No test for round-robin fixed-host override or unavailable/busy override cases

The PR claims to fix fixed-host date overrides for round-robin events, but the only added test checks that a personal-event override returns the same UTC slots in two invitee timezones. There is no coverage for fixed vs loose hosts, for start==end unavailable days, or for busy bookings on override days, so the === bug and the early-return that skips busy checks are not caught.

Outside-working-hours test uses find so split shifts reject valid slots

The code uses `workingHours.find` to look for any entry where the slot is outside that entry and then rejects the slot. With multiple intervals on the same weekday (e.g. morning and afternoon), a slot that fits the second interval still matches the outside condition of the first interval, so find succeeds and the valid slot is incorrectly rejected.

Override offset parses via toString and crashes when timeZone missing

The override conversion does `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)`. TimeRange.timeZone is optional and can be undefined, in which case tz() is invalid, and toString() round-trips through server locale strings losing millisecond/offset fidelity. This yields NaN or wrong utcOffset, shifting override start/end minutes and producing wrong slots or a runtime error.

Slots on date-override days return available without checking busy times

After detecting that a slot falls on a date-override day, checkIfIsAvailable does `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` before the busy-calendar check. That early return skips the `busy.every(...)` verification, so existing Cal bookings and external calendar blocks on override days are ignored and double-booking becomes possible.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unhandled KeyError on missing integration sender metadata

The check does integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with direct indexing. Metadata is not guaranteed to contain sender: build_integration only sets metadata["sender"] if state.get("sender"), and the pipeline only ever binds installation_id and github_authenticated_user, so pipeline-created integrations have no sender. Pre-existing/old integrations also lack it. When an orphaned Integration exists with no OrganizationIntegration, a retry hits this line and raises KeyError, producing a 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed.html error page and breaking reinstall flows.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing
OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

false_positives.candidate:
Empty installation_id bypasses App redirect

GitHubInstallation checks if installation_id is None, not if it is falsy. A request like ?installation_id= yields empty string, skips the redirect to the GitHub App URL, does Integration.objects.get(external_id="") and on DoesNotExist calls pipeline.next_step(). This proceeds to build_integration with an empty ID and a needless GitHub API call, instead of redirecting to install the App.

New installations bypass GitHub-user validation

In GitHubInstallation.dispatch when Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist the code returns pipeline.next_step() without comparing pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") to the installer. The sender check on lines 501-505 only runs when an Integration row already exists. Since the Integration row is created asynchronously by the GitHub webhook, an attacker can complete the pipeline before the webhook creates the row, or when the webhook is delayed/failed, and link an arbitrary installation_id without proving they installed the GitHub App. The existing tests prove this: assert_setup_flow creates an integration with no webhook/sender and succeeds.

OAuth token exchange and user lookup can raise 500

OAuthLoginView calls safe_urlopen for the access_token exchange and get_user_info for /user with no try/except. Network errors, non-2xx from GitHub, or an invalid/expired code/token will raise instead of returning a payload without access_token/login. Only missing keys in the parsed payload are handled. The consequence is a 500 on exactly the failure cases the PR description says should show the friendly Invalid installation request page.

Pipeline state poisoned before OAuth state validation

OAuthLoginView binds request.GET installation_id into pipeline state before checking if request.GET state equals pipeline.signature. A request with an invalid/forged state still mutates the stored installation_id before error() is returned. A subsequent legitimate retry that relies on pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id") will then use the attacker-controlled value, allowing fixation of the installation that will later be compared or built.

installation_not_found test no longer exercises 404

test_installation_not_found now sends state ddd023... which does not match the expected pipeline signature 9cae5e..., so OAuthLoginView rejects with Invalid installation request before GitHubInstallation/build_integration ever calls GET /app/installations. The stubbed 404 is never hit and the assertion was changed from The GitHub installation could not be found. The 404 handling in build_integration is therefore untested.

true_positives.golden_comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

true_positives.golden_comment: to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Raw datetime in Celery payload breaks serialization round-trip

In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py to_dict uses asdict and returns a raw datetime for queued, and src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py passes that dict as assignment_source_dict to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async. Celery task kwargs must be JSON-serializable; a datetime object either fails to enqueue or arrives as an ISO string. from_dict then does cls(**input_dict) with no string-to-datetime parsing and only catches ValueError/TypeError, so a string queued silently creates an object with queued as str or fails. Consequence: inbound-originated outbound syncs that now carry a source can fail to serialize or lose type instead of being cleanly filtered.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.

Malformed source fails open and re-creates sync loop

true_positives.golden_comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Inconsistent metric tag shard vs shards breaks dashboards

In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py the produce timer uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} while the wait_produce timer on the next line uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}, and segment_size_bytes uses "shard". The pluralization mismatch splits what should be one sharded metric family into different tag keys, breaking aggregation, dashboards, and alerts per shard.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Spawn flusher processes are never killed/terminated due to wrong isinstance

In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py the flusher creates processes via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, whose type is SpawnProcess, but restart and shutdown check isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), which on Linux is ForkProcess. A SpawnProcess is not an instance of ForkProcess (both only share BaseProcess), so the check is False in production. As a result process.kill() on hang/crash restart and process.terminate() in join() are never executed. Hung flusher processes leak and the replacement process flushes the same shards concurrently, causing duplicate Kafka produces, Redis contention, and unbounded process accumulation.

true_positives.golden_comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
join() abandons remaining flusher processes on timeout

In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py join() sets a deadline, joins next_step with the full timeout, then iterates over flusher processes and breaks out of the loop when the deadline is exceeded. Processes after the break are never waited on nor terminated, and if next_step consumed the whole timeout no flusher is even waited on. Hung or slow flushers are left running after rebalance/shutdown, leaking processes/threads and continuing to flush and produce.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

false_positives.candidate:
Test-mode flusher threads share mutable SpansBuffer with parent

In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py when produce_to_pipe is set the code uses threading.Thread with target partial(SpanFlusher.main, shard_buffer) and also stores the same shard_buffer object in self.buffers for the parent thread to call record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() in submit(). In production with real processes the child gets a pickled copy, but in tests both threads mutate/read the same SpansBuffer instance concurrently with flush_segments() and its any_shard_at_limit flag without locking. This is a data race that makes tests flaky and unrepresentative of production process isolation.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The magic number 50 for max_wait is used repeatedly throughout the tests. Consider extracting this as a named constant to improve maintainability.
The test test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling has a docstring that doesn't match the test implementation.

false_positives.candidate:
Partition lock creation is racy

OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock in src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py does get then setdefault on partition_locks with no global lock. Two threads adding the same new Partition concurrently can create two different Lock objects and then synchronize on different locks. That breaks the claimed per-partition mutual exclusion for add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable_offsets/mark_committed, allowing lost updates and wrong committable offsets, which causes duplicate processing or skipped commits.

Strategy close shuts down factory-shared pool, breaks rebalance

ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and reuses it for every strategy returned by create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close calls queue_pool.shutdown which kills all workers. On Arroyo rebalance/reassignment where the old strategy is closed and a new one is created from the same factory, the shared pool is left shut down with dead workers, so subsequent submits pile up unprocessed. Multiple concurrent strategies would also share one OffsetTracker with multiple commit threads double-committing.

Unbounded queues with no backpressure

FixedQueuePool creates each work queue as queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit/poll never blocks or returns a backpressure signal, despite the docstring claiming natural backpressure. If workers stall on a slow subscription, the Arroyo poll loop keeps submitting and memory grows without bound, leading to OOM and growing commit lag. poll only emits a gauge.

Worker swallows failures yet commits offsets

OrderedQueueWorker.run catches all Exceptions from result_processor, logs, then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in finally. Failed results are therefore treated as completed and the commit loop will commit past them, so failures are never retried and never reach Arroyo DLQ handling. ResultProcessor.__call__ already swallows exceptions, so mocking it to raise still gets committed, losing uptime results silently.

assert used for control flow on message type

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit uses assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue) to get partition/offset. Asserts are stripped with python -O, leaving partition/offset unbound, and for any non-BrokerValue message the AssertionError is caught by the blanket except and the message is silently dropped without tracking. FilteredPayload also hits assert not FilteredPayload inside decode_payload and relies on the exception path to mark progress, making normal filtering depend on exceptions.

terminate leaks commit thread

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.terminate in src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py sets shutdown_event and shuts down workers but never joins the commit_thread, unlike close. The daemon commit thread keeps running and keeps calling commit_function and mark_committed on the shared OffsetTracker after termination, causing use-after-terminate commits and thread leaks.

wait_until_empty/get_stats miss in-flight work

FixedQueuePool.get_stats and wait_until_empty use Queue.qsize, which counts only queued items not the item already removed by get and being processed by a worker. wait_until_empty can return True while offsets are still outstanding, and total_queued metrics undercount. Tests that wait on total_items==0 plus call counts are racy and can pass before processing or committing finishes, hiding ordering and commit bugs.

Denial cache key is ambiguous with underscore separator

In pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates userUID, action, name and parent with _ separators. UIDs, dashboard names and folder UIDs can contain _, so different tuples can produce the same key (e.g. name b_c parent d vs name b parent c_d). A collision causes one resource's denial to incorrectly deny a different resource.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.

false_positives.candidate:
Denial cache key omits identity type, cross-principal denial

In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check builds permDenialKey from namespace, UserUID, action, name and parent only, without IdentityType. Different identity types can share the same UID string, e.g. anonymous:0 yields UID 0 and render:0 also yields UID 0, and user vs service-account can share UID strings. A denial cached for one principal will therefore cause Check for a different principal with the same UID/action/resource to return Allowed:false without consulting the DB, incorrectly denying e.g. renderer reads that should always be allowed.

Denial cache short-circuit reintroduces stale deny after grant

In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check returns Allowed:false immediately on permDenialCache hit without requerying the DB, and caches every DB-computed denial for shortCacheTTL (30s). If permissions are granted after a denial was cached, the user continues to be denied until TTL expiry. This reintroduces the same staleness window the PR claims to fix, just moved from permCache to permDenialCache.

False deny from stale folder tree is cached in denial cache

In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check refreshes permissions from the DB on cached deny but reuses the same cached folderTree inside checkPermission/checkInheritedPermissions for both the cached and fresh evaluation. If folderCache is stale, the fresh evaluation can still return false, and that false is then stored in permDenialCache. The result stacks TTLs: a stale tree causes a denial entry that continues to deny even after the folder cache refreshes, extending the deny window beyond either TTL alone.

List serves stale cached permissions with no DB fallback

In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go List uses getCachedIdentityPermissions and if it hits returns that stale map directly to listPermission, only querying the DB on cache miss. Unlike Check which falls back to the DB when cached perms deny, List has no revalidation. A dashboard/folder created after the permCache entry was populated will be missing from List Items/Folders for up to 30s, so the stated goal of fetching newly created dashboards/folders is not fixed for list operations.

true_positives.golden_comment: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing React key for Grafana rules in filtered list

In FilterViewResults the rules.map destructures key but the grafana branch renders GrafanaRuleListItem without key={key} while the datasource branch passes it. Without stable keys React reuses DOM and component state incorrectly during infinite scroll and filter changes, causing wrong rows, lost focus, or actions opening for the wrong rule.

true_positives.golden_comment: RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.
