Silence drawer never opens for Prometheus-only rules

RuleActionsButtons now accepts prom-only Grafana rules with optional ruler rule and AlertRuleMenu enables Silence from prom abilities. handleSilence sets showSilenceDrawer true, but rendering is gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) where rule is the optional ruler DTO. In the list view rule is undefined so the condition is always false, SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer never mounts and clicking Silence does nothing.

false_positives.candidate:
Delete action hidden for Prometheus-only rules

canDelete is computed as OR of ruler and prom abilities, but the Delete menu item is gated on canDelete && rulerRule. With only promRule in the list view rulerRule is undefined so Delete never appears even with permission, making Grafana rules undeletable from the list. The handler signature also still requires a ruler DTO so no prom-aware delete path exists.

Duplicate allowed for cloud rules via Grafana permissions

useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities maps skipToken to undefined, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities still returns Duplicate as supported with allowed based on Grafana create permission even when rule is undefined. AlertRuleMenu calls it with skipToken for non-Grafana rules and ORs with the ruler result, so a user with Grafana create but without external write permission gets Duplicate enabled for Mimir/Loki/Cortex rules.

Export disabled for Grafana recording rules

In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities ModifyExport is [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed] where isAlertingRule is true only for alerting type. The ruler version used isGrafanaManagedAlertRule which is true for both alerting and recording. As a result Grafana recording rules always report export unsupported and lose the Export menu item.

Federated rules no longer treated as immutable

useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously checked isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) to block Update/Delete/Pause for federated groups. It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities with only rulerRule and group identifier, which hardcodes isFederated to false. Rule view link drops returnTo navigation state

The previous list item built the detail href as /alerting/grafana/<uid>/view with a returnTo query so the detail page can navigate back to the list with filters. The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds the href without returnTo, so Back from rule details loses list context.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

false_positives.candidate:
Early interpolation defeats $__range split exclusion

runSplitQuery in querySplitting.ts now interpolates every query with applyTemplateVariables before calling querySupportsSplitting, which excludes queries containing the $__range variable because $__range must be interpolated per split on the backend with the split time range. Because the same interpolation expands macros like $__auto to concrete values as shown in the new test, it will also expand $__range before the guard is checked, so isQueryWithRangeVariable never matches. Range-variable queries that must not be split will then be time-split with a frozen full-range value baked into every chunk, returning wrong data.

Empty-after-interpolation queries are no longer dropped

Both runSplitQuery and runShardSplitQuery filter on raw query.expr truthiness before calling applyTemplateVariables. A query like $var that is non-empty before interpolation but interpolates to an empty string is therefore kept. In the shard path this is a regression because the old code interpolated with interpolateVariablesInQueries first and then filtered, so variable-to-empty queries were dropped. The kept empty queries now go to fetchLabelValues for __stream_shard__ and to runQuery with an empty selector, causing backend errors and wasted shard requests. Filtering must also happen after interpolation.

Shard path interpolates template variables twice

runShardSplitQuery in shardQuerySplitting.ts now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on every target, then passes the already-interpolated targets to runSplitQuery in querySplitting.ts which calls applyTemplateVariables again on the same queries (with shard selector added). The updated test expects 5 applyTemplateVariables calls for a single query, proving the double pass. The second pass re-applies scopedVars and request.filters including ad-hoc filters to an expression that already contains them, which duplicates ad-hoc filter clauses, re-expands values containing $ and wastes work. Interpolation should happen once or the second pass must be skipped.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
New ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil request

ContextualLoggerMiddleware in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go dereferences req without a nil check, e.g. req.PluginContext in QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics. LoggerMiddleware in the same package explicitly guards with if req == nil, proving nil requests are considered possible. true_positives.golden_comment: The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Plugin request log loses traceID correlation

LoggerMiddleware in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go previously added traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext to the Plugin Request Completed log. The PR removes that logic and the replacement instrumentContext in contextual_logger_middleware.go only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname, never traceID. true_positives.golden_comment: The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TestLogger.FromContext discards log observations

TestLogger.FromContext in pkg/plugins/log/fake.go returns a brand-new TestLogger instead of the receiver. LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info, so with the fake the Info/Warn/Error call is recorded on a throwaway instance while the original instance under test still shows zero Calls. Tests asserting on the injected logger cannot observe the log, causing false negatives and hiding regressions in log content.

false_positives.candidate:
MetricsMiddleware panics on nil request

MetricsMiddleware in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go dereferences req without a nil check, e.g. req.Queries in QueryData and req.PluginContext / req.Body in CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics. LoggerMiddleware guards if req == nil, showing nil is expected. Since MetricsMiddleware is ordered outer to LoggerMiddleware, a nil request causes a nil-pointer panic in metrics code before Logger's guard is reached.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Count-then-insert race allows exceeding device limit

CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the limit with a separate CountDevices query followed by an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT/ON DUPLICATE KEY if count is below the limit, otherwise an UPDATE. There is no transaction, lock, or unique-count constraint between the check and the insert. Two concurrent requests for different new devices can both observe count below the limit and both insert, permanently exceeding the configured limit.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache-before-DB lets blocked devices bypass device limit on retry

tagDeviceUI in AnonDeviceService inserts the device CacheKey into localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice, and returns nil immediately on cache hit without touching the DB. When the limit is reached the first TagDevice for a new device returns ErrDeviceLimitReached and denies auth, but the key stays cached. The next request for the same blocked device hits the cache, returns success, and anonymous auth is allowed. The limit therefore only blocks the first request per 29-minute cache window.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

false_positives.candidate:
Anonymous auth now blocks synchronously on device tagging with no timeout

Authenticate previously tagged the device in a background goroutine with a 2-minute timeout using a detached context, so slow DB never blocked login. This change calls TagDevice synchronously on the request context with no timeout, and TagDevice now does a COUNT plus an upsert when a limit is configured. Every cache-miss anonymous login now pays that DB latency, and a slow or hung DB will stall anonymous authentication instead of being best-effort.

No test that existing devices can still update after limit reached

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only verifies that a second distinct device is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached when the limit is 1. It never verifies the intended allowed path that an already-counted device within the 30-day window can still be updated via updateDevice when the limit is reached. A regression breaking updates for existing devices while blocking new ones would not be caught.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Leftover error-level debug logging with full ID lists

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go logs at Error level on every cleanup batch in CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags, including the full ids slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, e.g. 32767 IDs) plus cond and err which is nil on success. This floods error logs with hundreds of KB per batch, triggers error alerts for normal operation, and wastes CPU. These are leftover debug statements and should be removed or demoted to Debug without dumping IDs.

true_positives.golden_comment: The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unrelated cleanup interval change from 10m to 1m

pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go changes the background ticker from time.Minute*10 to time.Minute*1. This runs all cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) 10x more often, increasing DB/CPU load and potentially worsening the MySQL deadlock this PR tries to fix. The PR description never mentions this change, so it looks like leftover debug code and should be reverted.

false_positives.candidate:
Quadratic string building for large SQLite IN clause

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go builds the SQLite DELETE IN list with values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) inside a loop over ids. This copies the growing string on every iteration, giving O(n^2) time and allocations. With batch sizes up to 32767 as in the new test this builds a ~200KB statement by copying gigabytes total, slowing cleanup. Use strings.Builder, strings.Join, or strconv.AppendInt instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Delete discards per-request logger when installing context

Delete builds `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` but then does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `log`. Downstream storage calls and any `klog.FromContext` logs lose name/kind/method fields, inconsistent with Create/Get/List/Update/DeleteCollection which install the enriched logger, harming correlation and debugging.

true_positives.golden_comment: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
DeleteCollection legacy result recorded as storage metric

The background goroutine for DeleteCollection calls `recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` for the `Legacy.DeleteCollection` result instead of `recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy latency and errors are attributed to the storage histogram and legacy metrics are never emitted for this method, corrupting SLOs and hiding legacy failures. All other async paths correctly call `recordLegacyDuration`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Delete success records object name as kind metric label

On successful storage delete the code calls `recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, ...)` where `name` is the object name like `foo`, while the error path and all other methods pass `options.Kind`. The `kind` label will get unbounded high-cardinality values (one series per object name), exploding Prometheus series and breaking dashboards/alerts that expect kind. It should be `options.Kind`.

false_positives.candidate:
Async legacy failures are never logged

All four background legacy writes only call `recordLegacyDuration`/`recordStorageDuration` and drop the error. There is no `log.Error` with name/kind/UID. Operators will not see why the legacy safety copy failed in logs, unlike the previous synchronous code which logged legacy errors. At minimum log the async legacy error with identifying fields.

Async legacy write derives context from cancelled request context

Create (and Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) spawns `go func()` then does `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`, where `ctx` is the incoming request context. The method returns immediately, the apiserver cancels the request context, and any child derived from it is cancelled immediately. The background Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection will therefore almost always run with a cancelled parent and fail/timeout, so the legacy copy is never kept in sync despite mode 3 promising best-effort legacy writes. Use a detached context like `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or `context.Background()` for the async work.

Create/Update storage errors recorded as legacy metrics

When `Storage.Create` fails the code calls `recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` and Update does the same on line 129 for `Storage.Update` failure. A storage failure is counted as a legacy failure with the storage start time, so storage error rate/latency is missing and legacy error rate is inflated. The error paths should call `recordStorageDuration` like Delete and DeleteCollection do.

Mode3 tests do not verify async legacy dual-write

Mode3 write tests return immediately after the synchronous storage call and never wait for the background legacy goroutine (no sleep/Eventually/AssertCalled). Delete and DeleteCollection tests set no legacy expectation at all, and legacy and storage share the same `*mock.Mock` so `Create/Update/Delete` calls cannot be attributed to a store. Tests pass even if legacy is never written (masking the cancelled-context bug above) and are flaky if the goroutine runs after the test finishes and hits an unexpected mock call.

Update re-invokes UpdatedObjectInfo for legacy causing divergence

Update forwards the same `objInfo` to `Storage.Update` and then asynchronously to `Legacy.Update`. Each store calls `UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` with its own different `old` object. If the transformer is not idempotent or depends on old resourceVersion/spec, the two stores compute different new objects or one fails with conflict. The previous implementation fetched the updated object once and reused it via `updateWrapper` so legacy got the storage result. Legacy should be written with the object returned from storage, not by re-executing user logic against stale legacy state, otherwise storage and legacy diverge.

true_positives.golden_comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing second cache check after acquiring write lock causes thundering herd

GetWebAssets does a fast-path check under RLock and if it misses acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu in write mode, but it never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock. If N goroutines concurrently observe a nil cache before the first load finishes, each will queue on the write lock and each will re-read assets-manifest.json/CDN and overwrite the global. The consequence is redundant disk/network I/O on cold start, wasted work, and different callers getting different pointers when one shared load would suffice.

true_positives.golden_comment: In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Failed load overwrites good cache with nil

GetWebAssets unconditionally executes entryPointAssetsCache = result even when the load failed and result is nil with err non-nil. In Dev mode the read bypasses the cache but the write still overwrites it, so one transient failure reading assets-manifest.json discards the previously good cached EntryPointAssets shared by all goroutines. Subsequent callers then see a nil cache and fail or must reload until a later success. The global should only be updated on success (err == nil and result != nil) to preserve the last good value.

false_positives.candidate:
Exclusive lock held across file and network I/O blocks all readers

GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu with Lock and defers Unlock, so the exclusive lock is held across readWebAssetsFromFile and readWebAssetsFromCDN, which perform file-system reads and HTTP fetches plus GetContentDeliveryURL. While the writer holds the lock, every other caller blocks even for RLock fast-path cache hits. In Dev mode every call takes the write lock, so concurrent requests fully serialize on disk I/O. This adds latency and contention; the load should happen outside the lock with a second check/singleflight and the lock held only to publish the result.

true_positives.golden_comment: The enableSqlExpressions function has flawed logic that always returns false, effectively disabling SQL expressions unconditionally:
true_positives.matched_candidate:
enableSqlExpressions has inverted check and always returns false via dead branches

In pkg/expr/reader.go enableSqlExpressions() computes enabled as negation of FlagSqlExpressions then returns false in both the if branch and fallthrough. The flag check is dead code and the negation obscures intent. Consequence: the disable looks like a logic mistake, inviting a future cleanup to flip one return to true and silently re-enable the DuckDB RCE/LFI path fixed for CVE-2024-9264; it should be an unconditional false with an explicit security comment.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The DB methods NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/db.go return hardcoded 'not implemented' errors after removing the go-duck dependency.

false_positives.candidate:
Empty SQL result never returns NoData, always overwritten with TableData

In pkg/expr/sql_command.go Execute() sets rsp.Values to mathexp.NoData when frame.Rows()==0 and then unconditionally overwrites rsp.Values with mathexp.TableData on the next lines. The NoData assignment is dead code and never observed by callers. Consequence: downstream no-data/alerting logic that distinguishes NoData from TableData will misclassify empty SQL results as data tables.

Security disable of SQL expressions has no regression test

This PR disables SQL expressions to fix critical RCE/LFI CVE-2024-9264 by gating pkg/expr/reader.go ReadQuery for QueryTypeSQL and stubbing pkg/expr/sql DB, but adds no test verifying that ReadQuery, NewSQLCommand/TablesList, and Execute reject SQL input even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled. Consequence: a one-line future change to the stub or gate can silently reintroduce remote code execution/file access with no automated guard.

tablesFromAST indexes ast[0] without empty check causing panic

In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go tablesFromAST() does flatten.Flatten(ast[0], ...) without checking len(ast) > 0. If the unmarshalled JSON is an empty array, null, or otherwise yields zero elements, this panics with index out of range. Consequence: a crafted SQL expression that produces such JSON crashes the handler/goroutine, a denial-of-service robustness bug that should be a returned error instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Check-then-act race allows duplicate builds for same index

getOrCreateIndex does GetIndex and if nil calls build without per-key singleflight. Previously bleve BuildIndex held a global lock for the whole build so duplicates were serialized. Now it only locks the final map insert. Two goroutines for the same NamespacedResource from parallel init, Search, or watch handling can both see nil and both run ListIterator plus bleve.New. This wastes work, double-increments IndexTenants and IndexedKinds metrics, leaks the loser index with last-writer-wins, and for file-backed indexes concurrently creates the same directory which fails with index already exists or lock contention.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TotalDocs iterates cache map without lock while builds write concurrently

bleveBackend.BuildIndex now only holds cacheMu for the final cache insert so many builds run in parallel, and GetIndex uses RLock. TotalDocs loops over b.cache with no lock at all. Concurrent iteration with concurrent map writes is a data race and can panic with concurrent map iteration and map write. It is called at the end of init and can run concurrently with on-demand builds from Search or watch events.

false_positives.candidate:
Data race on shared counter and error in parallel index init

In searchSupport.init the errgroup goroutine does totalBatchesIndexed++ and _, _, err = s.build(...) where totalBatchesIndexed and err are outer variables shared by all workers. With initWorkers > 1 this is concurrent unsynchronized read-modify-write and concurrent writes to the same err variable. It triggers the race detector, corrupts the indexed count reported in the span, and can lose or overwrite build errors so group.Wait returns the wrong error.

Eager Init blocks NewResourceServer on full index build

NewResourceServer now calls s.Init synchronously, which runs lifecycle init plus full search index build over all namespaces before returning. The PR description says the build takes too long for a gRPC context. Doing it synchronously in the constructor moves the same long blocking work to startup, delaying readiness and risking startup timeouts. On error it returns nil without calling the cancel func for the internal context, leaking that context.

Postgres storage-server test skipped instead of fixed

The change adds a skip for GRAFANA_TEST_DB=postgres in TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer with a TODO. This removes integration coverage for the storage server target on postgres, so regressions in the unified storage startup path on postgres will not be caught in CI.

Search watch goroutine leaks and panics on closed channel

searchSupport.init creates watchctx as context.Background with a comment new context and then runs for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) } with no ok check and no exit on cancellation. When the sql backend poller exits it closes the channel, so receives return nil forever. handleEvent dereferences evt.Type and evt.Key and will panic on nil, otherwise it busy-loops. The Background context is never cancelled so the goroutine also leaks on shutdown and loses tracing and admin claims.

Stop shutdown guard is dead after removing lazy Init checks

server.Stop sets s.initErr to service is stopping/stopped to make future calls fail. Previously every RPC called s.Init which returned that stored error. This PR removes all Init calls from Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob and GetBlob. Nothing now reads the value written by Stop, so the server keeps serving new requests after Stop instead of rejecting them, breaking graceful shutdown.

Trace context still discarded in bleve BuildIndex

The PR claims to fix trace propagation by keeping the Start context, and search.go and GetResourceStats were changed to ctx, span. bleveBackend.BuildIndex still does _, span := tracer.Start and discards the child context, so the builder callback and ListIterator inside the build are not children of the BuildIndex span. The same pattern remains in sql backend WriteEvent, ReadResource and ListIterator, so propagation is only partially fixed.

true_positives.golden_comment: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Test cleanup uses literal "alias" instead of created alias, leaking IdPs

The new test creates idp-alias-0..20 in a loop but registers cleanup as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove with the literal string "alias" instead of the loop variable. That cleanup removes nothing, so 20+ brokers remain in the realm. Leftover brokers pollute counts asserted in the same test (5/6/10/11) and any later tests using the realm, causing flakiness. Same pattern appears for org-idp creation and idp-alias-20.

false_negatives.golden_comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.

false_positives.candidate:
Generic login paths re-check only isEnabled, allowing stale hidden brokers to show

The specific-organization branch filters organization brokers by isEnabled() and !isLinkOnly() and !isHideOnLogin() and brokerPublic. The ORG_ONLY-without-org and ALL branches that use cached getForLogin() filter only by isEnabled(). If the login cache is stale or racy for hideOnLogin, linkOnly or brokerPublic, those stale IdPs remain in the cached id set, resolve successfully via getById(), pass the isEnabled() check, and are rendered on the login page when they should be hidden.

removeAll() does not invalidate login caches

removeAll() only registers invalidation for the count key and delegates, leaving realm .idp.login.* entries and org-id list queries in the cache. If removeAll() is ever called without deleting the realm, subsequent getForLogin() returns deleted brokers. It should invalidate login keys the same way create/remove do.

update() uses organization-aware wrapper for login invalidation, missing invalidations when org disabled

update() loads the original with getById(), which returns an organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() is false when its organization is disabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() decides with getLoginPredicate() which includes isEnabled(), so for an IdP in a disabled org both original and updated test as non-login. Changes to hideOnLogin, linkOnly or brokerPublic while the org is disabled therefore skip invalidation, leaving stale internalIds in the .idp.login caches. After the org is re-enabled OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), so a now-hidden, link-only or non-public broker from the stale list is displayed on the login page.

true_positives.golden_comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getBouncyCastleProvider returns default KeyStore provider instead of BouncyCastle

The method contract is to return the BouncyCastle security provider, but the implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which on a standard JDK is SUN or SunJSSE, not BouncyCastle. Callers expecting BouncyCastle-specific behavior will get the wrong provider. WildFlyElytronProvider returns null when there is no BouncyCastle provider; this implementation should do the same or throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning a misleading provider.

true_positives.golden_comment: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations
true_positives.matched_candidate:
New abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations

CryptoProvider added abstract method int order() with no default implementation. Any out-of-tree custom CryptoProvider compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration sorts by CryptoProvider::order, and will fail to compile against the new interface. As a public SPI this is a binary and source incompatible change. It should be a default method returning a sensible default.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.

false_positives.candidate:
ECDSA integer conversion silently truncates oversized and negative values

asn1derToConcatenatedRS decodes r/s with new BigInteger(bytes) which accepts negative integers, then integerToBytes truncates to qLength by copying the last qLength bytes without checking the dropped bytes. A DER value larger than the curve size or negative will be silently truncated to a different valid-looking value instead of throwing IOException. This masks invalid signatures, accepts non-canonical encodings, and can cause incorrect verification decisions. Dropped bytes must be verified to be zero and negatives rejected.

Equal-order providers selected nondeterministically, losing fail-fast

Previously multiple CryptoProviders on the classpath threw IllegalStateException. Now providers are sorted by order() reversed and the first is silently used, with others only logged at debug. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so if any two are present the winner depends on ServiceLoader iteration order which is classpath order dependent. This can silently swap FIPS for non-FIPS or vice versa with no warning, violating compliance expectations and hiding misconfiguration.

Test reuses P-256 key for ES384/ES512 and never verifies signature

The test generates one EC key pair with the default curve, typically P-256, and reuses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512 while only varying the target concatenated length. For ES384 and ES512 the conversion just zero-pads, so the round-trip assert passes without exercising real P-384 or P-521 sizes. It also only checks round-trip equality and never calls Signature.verify on the re-encoded DER, so a conversion that produces cryptographically invalid DER would still pass.

concatenatedRSToASN1DER lacks length validation and throws AIOOBE

The method assumes the input signature length equals signLength and immediately does System.arraycopy with len = signLength/2 without validation. A caller passing a truncated, overlong, or odd signLength gets ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of the declared IOException, and odd lengths are silently mishandled by integer division. It should validate signature != null, signature.length == signLength, and signLength even, and throw IOException otherwise.

readSequence does not enforce exact length and ignores trailing data

readSequence loops while length > 0 subtracting each element size but never checks that length ends at exactly zero and never checks that no bytes remain after the sequence. An inner element that overruns the declared outer length makes length negative and the loop exits successfully, and trailing garbage after the sequence is ignored. DER signature parsing must be strict and reject overlong, short, or trailing-data encodings to avoid malleability.

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Permission cleanup disabled and broken for V2

AdminPermissions.registerListener now only runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ V1 is enabled. With only V2 enabled, deletion of clients, roles and groups leaks V2 authorization resources and policies because setPermissionsEnabled is never called. With both V1 and V2 enabled, management returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client, role or group will fail with 500.

true_positives.golden_comment: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getClientsWithPermission never finds per-client resources

AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with only name and owner and never sets the Resource type, so their type is null. ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission enumerates candidates with findByType for Clients type, which only matches the single all-clients resource. Per-client grants are therefore never enumerated, and the global resource name Clients which is not a client id would be added to the result, so filtered client listing with per-client permissions returns empty or wrong results.

true_positives.golden_comment: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
NPE when all-clients resource is missing in per-client check

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String) when no per-client resource is found it falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource for Clients. That helper can return null, for example on upgraded realms without a Clients resource or if it was deleted. The code then calls findByResource(server, resource) with null without a null check, causing NullPointerException and HTTP 500 on admin client endpoints instead of safely denying access.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

false_positives.candidate:
Global canView ignores MANAGE grant

ClientPermissionsV2.canView without arguments returns true only for view permission, while canView for client scopes checks view or manage and per-client canView is true via canConfigure and canManage. An admin granted only manage on all clients will have canManage true but canView false, so global list and view checks deny managers who should be able to view. This is inconsistent with the transitive manage-implies-view behavior expected for users and scopes.

Global client grant ignored when per-client resource exists

ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String) evaluates only one resource: if a per-client resource exists it evaluates only that resource, otherwise it evaluates the all-clients resource. If a per-client resource was created for one scope like view, a check for another scope like manage or map-roles on the same client will evaluate only the per-client policies and ignore a valid all-clients grant, incorrectly denying access. Correct authorization requires OR of per-object and all-type grants.

NPE on invalid resourceType in getScope

AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope does SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that resourceType exists. If resourceType is null or unknown the get returns null and getScopes throws NullPointerException resulting in HTTP 500. It should throw ModelValidationException with 400 like other schema validations for bad permission input.

V2 evaluator throws 500 for unsupported operations

ClientPermissionsV2 implements methods like canExchangeTo, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource and getPermissions by throwing raw UnsupportedOperationException. When admin REST management endpoints or token-exchange checks call these in V2 mode the exception becomes HTTP 500 instead of a proper deny or 400 error, breaking API contract and availability.

Wrong Javadoc for void require methods

ClientPermissionEvaluator documents void methods requireView and requireViewClientScopes as Returns true if canView returns true. They return void and throw ForbiddenException on denial. The incorrect contract misleads callers into expecting a boolean result instead of exception-based enforcement.

getResourceName does not handle Clients type

AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName special-cases only Users to return All users or username. For Clients it falls through to resource.getDisplayName, but per-client resources created by getOrCreateResource have no display name set and are named by internal UUID. Admin UI and permission display for client permissions will therefore show null or UUID instead of All clients or clientId.

init does not migrate existing realms for new Clients type

AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns early if the admin-permissions client already exists, so realms created before this change never get the new Clients scopes and all-clients resource. Creating a client permission on such realms then fails scope lookup with ModelException No scopes found, and global client checks return false. Upgrade needs to add missing scopes and type resources to existing clients.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Incorrect method call for exit codes. The picocli.exit() method calls System.exit() directly, which is problematic:
Need to add changelog/release notes documenting the exit code change and migration guidance

false_positives.candidate:
Default strategy test deployment omits required rolling-updates flag

In UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment the method returns early when updateStrategy is null without enabling the rolling-updates feature, while the non-null path enables it via FeatureSpec. The operator docs in this same PR state the feature must be enabled otherwise the Operator will fail. Consequence: the parameterized runs with null strategy deploy a Keycloak CR without the required flag, so reconciliation will fail or will test different behavior than documented, invalidating testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount for the default strategy.

Feature gate only tested for metadata and exit codes never asserted

UpdateCommandDistTest adds testFeatureNotEnabled only for update-compatibility metadata, with no equivalent test for the check subcommand which has the same gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck. It also only asserts stderr text and never asserts exit code 4 for disabled feature, and testWrongVersions never asserts exit code 3 for recreate. This PR changes RECREATE exit from 4 to 3 and adds 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED, and automation relies on those codes. Consequence: a missing gate on check or a wrong exit code regression would not be caught by tests.

Test helper overwrites enabled features instead of appending

In UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment the code calls setEnabledFeatures(List.of(rolling-updates key)). That replaces the entire enabled-features list coming from getTestKeycloakDeployment instead of adding to it. Consequence: any features already enabled on the base deployment are silently dropped, so the test runs with the wrong feature set and can false-pass or false-fail.

true_positives.golden_comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Global group canManage incorrectly accepts view scope

In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() the fallback check is hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) on the all-groups resource, identical to canView(). This means an admin with only the view scope on Groups passes requireManage(), which guards create top-level group, delete and other manage operations. A view-only delegated admin can therefore create, update and delete groups, which is a privilege escalation.

true_positives.golden_comment: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Group view permission scan uses resource ID instead of group ID

In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission the code iterates resources of type Groups and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). For admin permissions, resource name equals the group ID and resource ID is a generated UUID. The lookup must use getName(), as V1 does with getName().substring(prefix). Using getId() means the per-group evaluation looks up a non-existent resource and the returned set contains authz UUIDs instead of group IDs, so user search filtered by UserModel.GROUPS returns empty or wrong results for group-scoped admins.

false_positives.candidate:
Missing null check for all-groups resource causes NPE on upgrade

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource for Groups and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without checking for null. Realms upgraded from before Groups existed, or realms where the resource server is not fully initialized, have no Groups type resource, so resource is null and the call throws NullPointerException, crashing every group permission check. UserPermissionsV2 line 111 has the same unchecked pattern.

Per-group check shadows all-groups permission

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission loads resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) and only if it is null falls back to the all-groups resource. If a per-group resource exists at all, for example created for a different admin, the all-groups permission is never evaluated. An admin with MANAGE or VIEW on all groups is then denied for that specific group despite the all-groups grant. The same pattern exists for users, breaking the expected all-users/all-groups transitive semantics.

Per-user check shadows all-users permission

UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission loads resourceStore.findByName(server, user.getId()) and only if null falls back to the all-users resource. If a per-user resource exists for the target user, for example created for another admin, the all-users permission is never evaluated. An admin with MANAGE or VIEW on all users loses access to that user, so creating any single-user permission revokes all-users access for other admins.

Scope deduplication via Set does not work

AdminPermissionsSchema.init collects new ScopeRepresentation objects into a Set to get rid of duplicities, but ScopeRepresentation does not implement equals/hashCode so each new instance is distinct. Scopes like manage and view that appear in Clients, Groups and Users types remain duplicated in the list passed to RepresentationToModel.toModel, causing duplicate scope creation attempts or failures when first enabling admin permissions.

getResourceName does not handle Groups type

AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName only special-cases Users, returning All users or the username, and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Group resources store the group ID as name with no displayName, so group permissions resolve to null or blank names in the admin UI and APIs. The new Groups type needs an All groups case and group name resolution like users.

getScope NPE on unknown resource type

AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope does SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that resourceType exists. A null or unknown resourceType causes NullPointerException instead of ModelValidationException, turning a bad admin API request into a 500 error.

requireManageMembers javadoc references wrong method

The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership returns false, duplicating the comment on requireManageMembership. It should reference canManageMembers. Readers cannot tell which check is enforced without reading the implementation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The translation is in Italian instead of Lithuanian. This should be translated to Lithuanian to match the file's locale (messages_lt.properties).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Lithuanian message replaced with Italian text

The totpStep1 value in the Lithuanian account bundle is now the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian instructions for OTP setup. The edit was meant to remove HTML links but copied the wrong language.

true_positives.golden_comment: The totpStep1 value uses Traditional Chinese terms in the Simplified Chinese file (zh_CN), which is likely incorrect for this locale. Please verify the locale‑appropriate translation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Simplified Chinese file uses Traditional characters

The new totpStep1 value in the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) account bundle uses Traditional characters such as mobile-phone and application words written in Traditional form. Users with Simplified Chinese locale will see Traditional text. The file should use Simplified characters like the surrounding entries.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The anchor sanitization logic has a potential issue where it consumes English matcher groups without proper validation. If the translated text has more anchor tags than the English text, this could lead to incorrect validation results.
The method name 'santizeAnchors' should be 'sanitizeAnchors' (missing 'i').
Field HTML_TAGS should be declared as 'private static final' following Java naming conventions for constants

false_positives.candidate:
Anchor mismatch error lacks key and file

The message added for a changed anchor contains only the tag text and the words in original string, without the message key or file name. The Illegal HTML message in the same file includes both key and file. When verification fails on a large bundle the maintainer cannot locate the offending key without reproducing locally.

HTML detection is case-sensitive

The patterns for detecting HTML and anchor tags only match lowercase tag names. HTML tag names are case-insensitive, so an English source containing uppercase tags like B or A would be classified as containing no HTML and select the wrong sanitizer policy, mishandling a matching translation.

Illegal HTML fixture is truncated

The fixture value ends with open-div without the final closing bracket. The test therefore exercises a truncated tag rather than a proper disallowed element. It can pass for the wrong reason and does not document the intended illegal-tag case.

Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text

The loginTotpStep1 value in the Lithuanian login bundle is now the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian instructions. The change was meant to strip anchor tags but inserted the wrong language.

Missing English file crashes verifier with RuntimeException

If the English counterpart file cannot be opened, verifySafeHtml throws an unchecked RuntimeException. The public verify method is declared to throw MojoExecutionException for IO problems. A single missing English file will therefore crash the theme-verifier plugin with a stack trace instead of producing a readable verification failure.

Missing anchors in translation are never detected

santizeAnchors only loops over anchor tags found in the translated value and checks each against English. It never checks that every anchor from the English source was consumed. A translation that deletes a required link entirely will therefore pass with no error, resulting in broken UI where the link is silently missing but the build stays green.

No positive test for valid translations

All tests assert that bad fixtures produce an error, but none asserts that good fixtures produce zero errors. For example there is no check that the valid English file or a translation with allowed formatting passes cleanly. A verifier that false-positives on every legitimate message would still pass the suite.

Verbatim compare causes false positive on br tag formatting

The verifier compares OWASP sanitizer output verbatim to the input. The sanitizer normalizes a self-closing break from br-slash form to br-space-slash form. A safe translation using the first form is therefore reported as Illegal HTML even though it is semantically identical. The PR had to rewrite more than twenty existing translations only to add that space, proving future contributions will be falsely rejected.

true_positives.golden_comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Constructor never null-checks rawTokenId

AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType) twice, the second with message "Null rawTokenId not allowed", and never checks rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and later encoded as the string "null" after ':' or causes NPE on decode, producing corrupt token IDs and misleading error messages.

true_positives.golden_comment: In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
isAccessTokenId matcher logic inverted and wrong offset

The matcher splits token ID on ':' then does if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false. It should reject when NOT equal and grant shortcut occupies chars 4-6 (substring 4,6) of the 6-char prefix session(0-1)+token(2-3)+grant(4-5). As written any 6-char prefix with a valid UUID passes regardless of grant, so tests for authorization_code, device, refresh and ciba grants never actually verify the encoded grant and give false confidence.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

false_positives.candidate:
Decoding untrusted token ID throws instead of returning UNKNOWN

getTokenContextFromTokenId returns UNKNOWN session/token/grant when there is no ':' (old UUID tokens) but throws IllegalArgumentException for wrong prefix length or unknown shortcuts. The input is the jti from a client-presented JWT, so a crafted or legacy ID containing ':' triggers an unhandled exception and 500/log spam. Handling should be consistent and return UNKNOWN for undecodable IDs.

Initial offline tokens encoded as online

Session type is derived only from userSession.isOffline() at initToken time. For an authorization-code flow requesting offline_access, the user session is still online when the access token is created and the online session is removed only afterwards in OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse. The first access token for an offline grant is therefore encoded as ONLINE while refreshed tokens are OFFLINE, defeating the stated optimization of avoiding double session lookup.

Lazy grant-map updates are non-atomic and unchecked

getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily do grantsByShortcuts.put plus grantsToShortcuts.put as two separate ConcurrentHashMap operations with no synchronization and no duplicate-shortcut validation. Concurrent first use can leave the two maps inconsistent, and a new grant reusing an existing shortcut silently overwrites the decode mapping, making future token IDs ambiguous.

Lightweight detection uses context client not token client

getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines lightweight vs regular via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient(). TokenManager.initToken already has the correct ClientModel parameter for the token being created. If context client differs from token client or is null, the encoded tokenType is wrong and initToken can NPE, breaking token issuance on a hot path that previously never touched the context client.

New abstract getShortcut breaks custom grant providers

Adding abstract String getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks source and binary compatibility for any third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation. Existing custom grants will fail compilation and throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when loaded. It should be a default method returning a safe fallback like "na".

Removed public copy constructor breaks compatibility

The public Context(Context context) copy constructor was deleted. Any existing custom grant code or extension that copied grant context with new Context(oldContext) will fail compilation and throw NoSuchMethodError at runtime. It should be retained as deprecated and delegate to field copies plus grantType.

Unknown grant aborts token creation instead of falling back

encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException when factory.getShortcutByGrantType returns null. It is called from TokenManager.initToken for every access token. Any token whose ClientSessionContext grant attribute is set to a value without a registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory, such as implicit/hybrid flows or custom values, will fail the whole token request with 500 instead of falling back to the existing "na" unknown-grant encoding.

grantType becomes stale after setFormParams and can NPE

Context captures grantType once in the constructor from formParams.getFirst("grant_type") without null-checking formParams, then setFormParams() replaces the map without updating grantType. If formParams is null construction NPEs, and if params are replaced the encoded grant will be the stale value, causing wrong grant shortcut in the access-token ID.

true_positives.golden_comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unchecked Optional.get() causes 500 on recovery login

In RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java at line 19, the constructor calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) then immediately does credentialModelOpt.get() without checking isPresent. A user-storage provider is allowed to implement CredentialInputValidator.isValid without exposing credentials via getCredentials(), or the credential may be missing/mismatched between federated and local stores. In that case this throws NoSuchElementException and produces a 500 error when rendering the recovery-code login form instead of a handled authentication failure.

true_positives.golden_comment: After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Federated getCredentials discards stored credential ID

In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java at line 237, getCredentials() builds the returned value via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) which creates a new CredentialModel with a fresh ID, discarding the ID assigned in updateCredential() to myUser.recoveryCodes. Any later operation by ID such as account-console DELETE /credentials/{id} or RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.removeStoredCredentialById() when all codes are used will use an ID that does not match the stored federated credential, so deletion silently fails and a stale credential remains.

false_positives.candidate:
Exhausted federated recovery credential never removed

In RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java at line 86, after successful validation the code loads the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() which now may return a federated credential and then calls removeStoredCredentialById() when allCodesUsed(). Federated credentials are managed via the UserStorageProvider disable path, which the bundled test provider does not implement for recovery codes, so for federated users this deletion is a no-op: exhausted codes remain stored and the addRequiredAction(CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES) logic dependent on removal breaks.

Federated recovery codes cannot be disabled/deleted

In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java at line 217, disableCredentialType() only handles OTP types and logs unsupported for anything else, and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() at line 254 only advertises OTP. As a result admin disableCredentialType and account-management deletion for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE are no-ops for federated users: federated recovery codes can never be removed via the supported APIs and remain valid.

Federated recovery-code validation does not consume codes

In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java at line 340, isValid() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only does generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...) and returns true without removing or marking the used code as consumed. The local keycloak-recovery-authn-codes provider makes codes single-use and tracks allCodesUsed() to force regeneration and deletion. With this implementation the same federated recovery code can be replayed indefinitely, allCodesUsed() never becomes true, and the test only logs in once so reuse is never caught.

Raw recovery codes sent to user storage in plaintext

In CredentialHelper.java at line 123, createRecoveryCodesCredential() serializes the raw generatedCodes list to JSON and passes it as the UserCredentialModel to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(), while the local path stores only hashed codes inside RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel. External user storage therefore persists recoverable plaintext recovery codes, as demonstrated by the test provider storing credentialData verbatim, so compromise of the external store yields all codes. Hashed material could be stored and verified like the local provider does.

getCredentials NPE for users not in federated map

In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java at line 232, getCredentials() does var myUser = getMyUser(user) then dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without a null check, while isConfiguredFor() and isValid() explicitly handle null. When the storage provider is enabled Keycloak calls getFederatedCredentialsStream/getCredentials for every user including purely local users not in the users map, so myUser is null and this throws NullPointerException, breaking credential listing and login for unrelated users.

true_positives.golden_comment: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Concurrent test thread is never joined and can leak/race

In tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a new Thread that loops calling groups(null,0,Integer.MAX_VALUE,true) and discards the handle via new Thread(...).start(). false_positives.candidate:
Partition lock creation is racy

OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock in src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py does get then setdefault on partition_locks with no global lock. Two threads adding the same new Partition concurrently can create two different Lock objects and then synchronize on different locks. That breaks the claimed per-partition mutual exclusion for add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable_offsets/mark_committed, allowing lost updates and wrong committable offsets, which causes duplicate processing or skipped commits.

Unbounded queues with no backpressure

FixedQueuePool creates each work queue as queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit/poll never blocks or returns a backpressure signal, despite the docstring claiming natural backpressure. If workers stall on a slow subscription, the Arroyo poll loop keeps submitting and memory grows without bound, leading to OOM and growing commit lag. poll only emits a gauge.

Strategy close shuts down factory-shared pool, breaks rebalance

ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and reuses it for every strategy returned by create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close calls queue_pool.shutdown which kills all workers. On Arroyo rebalance/reassignment where the old strategy is closed and a new one is created from the same factory, the shared pool is left shut down with dead workers, so subsequent submits pile up unprocessed. Multiple concurrent strategies would also share one OffsetTracker with multiple commit threads double-committing.

terminate leaks commit thread

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.terminate in src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py sets shutdown_event and shuts down workers but never joins the commit_thread, unlike close. The daemon commit thread keeps running and keeps calling commit_function and mark_committed on the shared OffsetTracker after termination, causing use-after-terminate commits and thread leaks.

Worker swallows failures yet commits offsets

OrderedQueueWorker.run catches all Exceptions from result_processor, logs, then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in finally. Failed results are therefore treated as completed and the commit loop will commit past them, so failures are never retried and never reach Arroyo DLQ handling. ResultProcessor.__call__ already swallows exceptions, so mocking it to raise still gets committed, losing uptime results silently.

assert used for control flow on message type

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit uses assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue) to get partition/offset. Asserts are stripped with python -O, leaving partition/offset unbound, and for any non-BrokerValue message the AssertionError is caught by the blanket except and the message is silently dropped without tracking. FilteredPayload also hits assert not FilteredPayload inside decode_payload and relies on the exception path to mark progress, making normal filtering depend on exceptions.

wait_until_empty/get_stats miss in-flight work

FixedQueuePool.get_stats and wait_until_empty use Queue.qsize, which counts only queued items not the item already removed by get and being processed by a worker. wait_until_empty can return True while offsets are still outstanding, and total_queued metrics undercount. Tests that wait on total_items==0 plus call counts are racy and can pass before processing or committing finishes, hiding ordering and commit bugs.

false_positives.candidate:
60-second eligibility cache returns stale upsampling decisions

is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches allowlist eligibility (True/False) for 60 seconds keyed only by org and projects. If the project allowlist changes, queries for up to 60s use the old decision and return raw count() when scaled upsampled_count() was required or vice versa, with errors scaled by 1/sample_rate (e.g. 10x). The invalidate_upsampling_cache helper defined in the same file is never called in the PR, so there is no invalidation path.

Error-focus check reads original HTTP query and only matches event.type:error

_is_error_focused_query inspects request.GET.get("query"), the original HTTP parameter, not the query string argument actually sent to Snuba. Dashboard-split code re-executes _get_event_stats with rewritten queries like (query) AND !event.type:transaction for errors and (query) AND event.type:transaction for transactions while request.GET is unchanged. The check also only matches substring event.type:error, so a discover errors-only query built from !event.type:transaction is treated as non-error and undercounts, while a transactions-only subquery issued when the HTTP query contained event.type:error is treated as error and sums sample_weight which does not exist for transactions.

upsampled_count sums nullable sample_weight without fallback and truncates

The new Discover function is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no null handling. Any error row without sample_weight (events written before sampling, backfills, mixed data) contributes 0/NULL instead of 1, so buckets undercount and can collapse to 0. toInt64 also truncates fractional weights, so a rate that does not evenly divide 1 (e.g. 0.33 -> weight ~3.03) is systematically biased low on every bucket. It should sum coalesced weights with rounding, e.g. sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1)).

Internal upsampled_count function exposed as public API

SnQLFunction upsampled_count is registered without private=True, unlike neighboring internal aggregates. That makes upsampled_count() directly queryable by any Discover user. Because it sums the internal sample_weight column, callers can invoke it on non-allowlisted projects or datasets where the column is missing or 1 and receive misleading scaled numbers, and can probe internal sampling state. Internal upsampling helpers should be private.

Column transform only handles exact count() and hardcodes alias

transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites a column whose lowercased stripped value equals exactly count(). Variants such as count() as foo, count_if, count_unique, or equations containing count() are left as raw counts, so a request mixes raw and scaled series in one response. When it does match it forces upsampled_count() as count, discarding the caller's alias and injecting AS syntax into RPC y_axes paths that expect bare aggregates, risking validation failures or mislabeled series.

Main upsampling entry point and cache behavior untested

The test class exercises only private helpers (_are_all_projects_error_upsampled, transform, _is_error_focused_query, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform) and never calls the public is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects. Cache-key construction, 60s staleness, hash instability, and dataset/request interaction therefore have zero unit coverage, and the SnubaParams fixture with start=None/end=None is never used, so the caching bugs shipped in this PR cannot be caught.

Unbounded limit/offset params allow DoS and invalid queries

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive allowing bypass

BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up with BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first using the raw user-supplied string with no downcasing or stripping, and the model validates uniqueness case-sensitively. Email delivery treats addresses case-insensitively in practice and users can add case changes or whitespace. An attacker blocked as bad@spam.com can sign up as BAD@spam.com or Bad@spam.com and miss the block, and admins can create logically duplicate block entries. Should normalize emails on save and lookup, e.g. with Email.downcase and strip.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same vulnerability: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` performs a case-sensitive email lookup, which allows blocked users to bypass the restriction by altering the casing of their email address.

false_positives.candidate:
Non-atomic match_count increment loses concurrent updates

BlockedEmail.should_block? does read-modify-write: record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save. Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email can interleave reads and overwrite each other, losing increments. The save also runs full validations including an extra uniqueness SELECT. Consequence is lost counts under load and wasted queries. Should use an atomic increment such as increment_counter or update_counters that bypasses validations.

change_email action bypasses blocked-email check

UsersController#change_email lowercases the new address, checks only whether another User already owns it, then creates an EmailToken and enqueues authorization without ever running EmailValidator or checking BlockedEmail.should_block?. An address rejected at signup as blocked can therefore still be adopted by an existing account via the email-change flow. Consequence is the blocklist is ineffective after account creation. The new address should be validated the same way as signup.

Wrong Ember dependent key prevents rejected-email UI update

emailValidation is declared dependent on accountEmail and rejectedEmails.@each. In Ember, @each observes properties of array items, not array membership; pushing a string with pushObject does not invalidate the computed property. The correct key is rejectedEmails.[] or length. After the server rejects an email and it is pushed into rejectedEmails, the validation still returns ok and submitDisabled stays false until the user edits the email, so the user can immediately resubmit the same blocked email repeatedly.

Shared mutable rejectedEmails array on prototype

CreateAccountController is extended with rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) as a prototype property. That single array instance is shared by all instances of the controller. Pushes of server-rejected emails leak across modal instances and persist after close/reopen, causing stale addresses to be treated as rejected for future unrelated signups. Mutable defaults should be created per-instance in init or reset when the modal opens.

The webhook looks up an existing credential with findFirst by userId+appId and updates that one row. Users can have multiple credentials for the same appId (e.g. two Google accounts, team vs user). findFirst picks an arbitrary row, so a sync can overwrite the wrong account's key and leave duplicates, corrupting calendar/video access.

false_positives.candidate:
Async legacy write derives context from cancelled request context

Create (and Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) spawns `go func()` then does `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`, where `ctx` is the incoming request context. The method returns immediately, the apiserver cancels the request context, and any child derived from it is cancelled immediately. The background Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection will therefore almost always run with a cancelled parent and fail/timeout, so the legacy copy is never kept in sync despite mode 3 promising best-effort legacy writes. Use a detached context like `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or `context.Background()` for the async work.

Update re-invokes UpdatedObjectInfo for legacy causing divergence

Update forwards the same `objInfo` to `Storage.Update` and then asynchronously to `Legacy.Update`. Each store calls `UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` with its own different `old` object. If the transformer is not idempotent or depends on old resourceVersion/spec, the two stores compute different new objects or one fails with conflict. The previous implementation fetched the updated object once and reused it via `updateWrapper` so legacy got the storage result. Legacy should be written with the object returned from storage, not by re-executing user logic against stale legacy state, otherwise storage and legacy diverge.

DeleteCollection legacy result recorded as storage metric

The background goroutine for DeleteCollection calls `recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` for the `Legacy.DeleteCollection` result instead of `recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy latency and errors are attributed to the storage histogram and legacy metrics are never emitted for this method, corrupting SLOs and hiding legacy failures. All other async paths correctly call `recordLegacyDuration`.

Create/Update storage errors recorded as legacy metrics

When `Storage.Create` fails the code calls `recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` and Update does the same on line 129 for `Storage.Update` failure. A storage failure is counted as a legacy failure with the storage start time, so storage error rate/latency is missing and legacy error rate is inflated. The error paths should call `recordStorageDuration` like Delete and DeleteCollection do.

Async legacy failures are never logged

All four background legacy writes only call `recordLegacyDuration`/`recordStorageDuration` and drop the error. There is no `log.Error` with name/kind/UID. Operators will not see why the legacy safety copy failed in logs, unlike the previous synchronous code which logged legacy errors. At minimum log the async legacy error with identifying fields.

Mode3 tests do not verify async legacy dual-write

Mode3 write tests return immediately after the synchronous storage call and never wait for the background legacy goroutine (no sleep/Eventually/AssertCalled). Delete and DeleteCollection tests set no legacy expectation at all, and legacy and storage share the same `*mock.Mock` so `Create/Update/Delete` calls cannot be attributed to a store. Tests pass even if legacy is never written (masking the cancelled-context bug above) and are flaky if the goroutine runs after the test finishes and hits an unexpected mock call.

getTokenContextFromTokenId returns UNKNOWN session/token/grant when there is no ':' (old UUID tokens) but throws IllegalArgumentException for wrong prefix length or unknown shortcuts. The input is the jti from a client-presented JWT, so a crafted or legacy ID containing ':' triggers an unhandled exception and 500/log spam. getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines lightweight vs regular via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient(). Any token whose ClientSessionContext grant attribute is set to a value without a registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory, such as implicit/hybrid flows or custom values, will fail the whole token request with 500 instead of falling back to the existing "na" unknown-grant encoding.

getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily do grantsByShortcuts.put plus grantsToShortcuts.put as two separate ConcurrentHashMap operations with no synchronization and no duplicate-shortcut validation. Concurrent first use can leave the two maps inconsistent, and a new grant reusing an existing shortcut silently overwrites the decode mapping, making future token IDs ambiguous.

false_positives.candidate:
Global client grant ignored when per-client resource exists

ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String) evaluates only one resource: if a per-client resource exists it evaluates only that resource, otherwise it evaluates the all-clients resource. If a per-client resource was created for one scope like view, a check for another scope like manage or map-roles on the same client will evaluate only the per-client policies and ignore a valid all-clients grant, incorrectly denying access. Correct authorization requires OR of per-object and all-type grants.

Global canView ignores MANAGE grant

ClientPermissionsV2.canView without arguments returns true only for view permission, while canView for client scopes checks view or manage and per-client canView is true via canConfigure and canManage. An admin granted only manage on all clients will have canManage true but canView false, so global list and view checks deny managers who should be able to view. This is inconsistent with the transitive manage-implies-view behavior expected for users and scopes.

AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope does SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that resourceType exists. If resourceType is null or unknown the get returns null and getScopes throws NullPointerException resulting in HTTP 500. It should throw ModelValidationException with 400 like other schema validations for bad permission input.

AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName special-cases only Users to return All users or username. For Clients it falls through to resource.getDisplayName, but per-client resources created by getOrCreateResource have no display name set and are named by internal UUID. Admin UI and permission display for client permissions will therefore show null or UUID instead of All clients or clientId.

AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns early if the admin-permissions client already exists, so realms created before this change never get the new Clients scopes and all-clients resource. Creating a client permission on such realms then fails scope lookup with ModelException No scopes found, and global client checks return false. ClientPermissionsV2 implements methods like canExchangeTo, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource and getPermissions by throwing raw UnsupportedOperationException. When admin REST management endpoints or token-exchange checks call these in V2 mode the exception becomes HTTP 500 instead of a proper deny or 400 error, breaking API contract and availability.
